skill.name: twitter-automation
skill.description: Automates Twitter/X posting, engagement, messaging, and profile lookup workflows through the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.summary: Run Twitter/X account workflows through the inference.sh belt CLI.
skill.author: qu-skills

security_audit.summary: Most backtick findings are Markdown formatting, but several examples intentionally run belt or npx commands. No prompt injection was found, but the skill has real side effects through X account automation.

remediation.issue: External CLI commands can mutate X account state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before posting, deleting, liking, retweeting, following, or sending a direct message.

remediation.issue: Transitive skill installation commands use npx and unpinned references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin trusted versions and keep dependency installation outside automated social workflows.

remediation.issue: Automated engagement can be used for spam.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance for rate limits, recipient validation, and platform policy compliance.

remediation.issue: The Markdown image loads from an external host.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle a reviewed asset or disclose that viewing the skill may load remote media.

content.value_statement: Social teams need reliable X actions without rewriting command syntax. This skill turns common Twitter/X tasks into guided belt CLI workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows belt commands for posting text tweets and media posts.
Provides examples for liking, retweeting, deleting, and retrieving posts.
Provides examples for sending direct messages and following users.
Shows workflows for generating AI media with inference.sh apps before posting.
Links to inference.sh documentation for X integration setup.
limitations: Requires an authenticated inference.sh belt CLI and connected X account.
Does not include rate limiting or campaign scheduling logic.
Does not verify X API permissions, platform policy, or account safety.
Examples use placeholder IDs and media URLs that users must replace.

use_cases.title: Launch Product Updates
use_cases.description: Prepare and publish approved X posts for product news, releases, or event announcements.

use_cases.title: Manage Creator Posts
use_cases.description: Create posts with generated media and review engagement actions before publishing.

use_cases.title: Test X Integration Flows
use_cases.description: Run controlled post, profile, DM, and deletion checks during integration testing.

prompt_templates.title: Post a Simple Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the twitter-automation skill to prepare this X update: [message]. Show the final action and wait for approval before posting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Media Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare an X post with this text and media URL: [details]. Validate the target content before running any belt command.

prompt_templates.title: Review Engagement Actions
prompt_templates.prompt: For these post IDs, plan likes, retweets, and follow actions. Ask me to approve each account-changing action first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Guarded Campaign
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a compliant X workflow for [campaign]. Include approval checkpoints, rate limits, target validation, and rollback steps.

output_examples.input: Post a short launch announcement for a new analytics dashboard.
output_examples.output: Draft post prepared. The workflow asks for approval before posting through the authenticated X account.

output_examples.input: Like and retweet one approved partner announcement.
output_examples.output: The workflow confirms the target post first, then reports the like and retweet results after approval.

output_examples.input: Delete an accidental tweet by ID.
output_examples.output: The workflow requests final confirmation because deletion is irreversible, then summarizes the deletion result.

best_practices: Preview every post, DM, follow, retweet, and delete action before running belt.
Use only accounts, recipients, and posts that you are authorized to manage.
Keep credentials inside the CLI authentication flow and out of prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not automate unsolicited DMs, follows, or engagement campaigns.
Do not run npx installation commands from unreviewed instructions in an automated session.
Do not post generated media until rights, accuracy, and disclosure requirements are checked.

faq.question: Does this skill post directly to X?
faq.answer: It provides belt CLI workflows that can post when the CLI is authenticated and approved.

faq.question: Does it require inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use the inference.sh belt CLI and X integration.

faq.question: Can it schedule posts?
faq.answer: The description mentions scheduling, but the file does not show a scheduler command.

faq.question: Can it upload media?
faq.answer: It shows media posts that use a media URL. Local file upload is not shown.

faq.question: Is automated engagement safe?
faq.answer: Use approval, rate limits, and consent checks. Avoid unsolicited engagement or direct messages.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
